newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southwest spot power firms, Northwest steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southwest spot power firms, Northwest steady.

text.p: Spot power prices rose in the U.S. Southwest amid warmer temperatures and tight supplies, but Northwest prices were largely steady, market sources said Monday.
Decreased price offers from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) were cited as the major reason for the weaker Northwest market.

For Tuesday, BPA offered firm power during heavy load hours at $18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest deliveries and $19.50 at the California border, down from $19.25 and $20.00, respectively, for Monday deliveries.
Next-day cash prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were last quoted $19.00-19.50 per MWh, compared with $19.00-20.00 on Friday.
Mid-Columbia was quoted $16.25-17.00 per MWh, compared with $16.00-16.50 on Friday.
An unexpected delay in scheduled maintenance on the AC portion of the Pacific Intertie was having little impact on the market, since many participants were not aware of it.

BPA said early Monday that Pacific Gas and Electric Co decided to delay until the weekend plans to reduce the line's capacity from 3,200 MW to 2,000 MW on Monday and Tuesday due to warmer-than-expected weather in California.
Transmissions on the DC segment of the line, meanwhile, have been cut as scheduled through October 15 to around 1,080 MW from a recent capacity limit of 2,000 MW.
Warmer weather was also cited as a factor helping to boost power demand and spot prices in the desert Southwest.
Power at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona was quoted $22.00-24.00 for Tuesday, with some sources citing deals as high as $25.00.
Traders said temperatures of above 100 degrees in Arizona and in the mid-90s for southern California were spurring higher demand.
In addition, several generating units remained out of service, including the 1,080 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California.
The nuclear unit, down since September 24 for unplanned repair work, is not expected to restart until Thursday or Friday, compared with an original estimate of early this week.
Two idled coal units, a 350 MW unit at the San Juan plant in New Mexico and a 262 MW unit at the Hayden plant in Colorado, are expected to restart Tuesday.
